open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes)”; accepting that binding can change the proof result without changing the flow version.
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same flow version can produce different results as referenced bindings change status?
options: Treat each distinct result as a value identified by the flow version plus the dependency state or result facts
Treat ProofResult as a mutable current result for the flow version
Require proof to remain invariant for a flow version
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computation as a value determined by the flow version and the binding state observed during that computation.

open_points.subject: M06 TrialCase capture after spool deletion
open_points.text: Capture excludes an execution “whose run was already released, since its spooled files are gone,” but K-10 and M22 remove spool bytes whenever any non-failed run ends, including a run ending `refused` or `cancelled`.
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, and how does eligibility differ between value-only inputs and inputs containing files whose spool bytes were removed?
options: Allow capture only while every required input payload still exists
Allow value-only capture after those endings but refuse capture requiring removed files
Refuse every capture after any run has ended
Retain files from any run containing a capturable failure
open_points.default_guess: Allow capture whenever all required inputs remain available; therefore allow durable value-only inputs but refuse cases requiring removed spool bytes.

open_points.subject: M26 EffectAttempt `not_applied` outcome
open_points.text: M26 allows `in_flight` → `not_applied` directly and says “Sending again after `not_applied` is a new attempt under a fresh approval,” while only resolution of an `unknown` outcome is specified to continue the run and potentially resend.
open_points.question: What happens to the node and run when an effect is known directly to be `not_applied`, rather than becoming `not_applied` through the owner's resolution of `unknown`?
options: Request fresh approval and wait to resend in the same run
End the node as failed with no same-run resend
Treat a valid not-applied service response as successful and continue with its outputs
Rest pending until a separate retry action is invoked
open_points.default_guess: Request a fresh approval and place the run in `awaiting_approval` for a new attempt.
